# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

## Overview

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
3. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
4. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
5. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
6. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill";
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**
- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**
- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**
- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

## After the Design

**Documentation:**
- Write the validated design to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Implementation:**
- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

1→# DuckDB Data Agent
     2→
     3→> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.
     4→
     5→[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)
     6→
     7→A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.
     8→
     9→## Features
    10→
    11→### General
    12→
    13→- **Dark / light mode** — Toggle between dark and light themes with the sun/moon button in the header; respects your OS preference on first visit and remembers your choice across sessions
    14→- **Internationalization (i18n)** — Switch between English and Traditional Chinese with the EN/中 toggle in the header; auto-detects your OS language on first visit and remembers your choice across sessions
    15→
    16→### SQL Playground
    17→
    18→- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
    19→- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
    20→- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
    21→- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
    22→- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
    23→- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
    24→- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types
    25→
    26→### AI Agent
    27→
    28→- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
    29→- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
    30→- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
    31→- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
    32→- **Edit & delete messages** — Hover over any user message to edit or delete it; editing re-sends the modified query with prior conversation as context, deleting rewinds the conversation to that point
    33→- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
    34→- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI
    35→
    36→## Getting Started
    37→
    38→### Prerequisites
    39→
    40→- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
    41→- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
    42→- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)
    43→
    44→### Installation
    45→
    46→```bash
    47→make install
    48→```
    49→
    50→Or install frontend and backend separately:
    51→
    52→```bash
    53→cd frontend && npm install
    54→cd backend && poetry install
    55→```
    56→
    57→### Configuration
    58→
    59→Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:
    60→
    61→```bash
    62→cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
    63→```
    64→
    65→Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:
    66→
    67→```
    68→ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
    69→ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
    70→```
    71→
    72→> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.
    73→
    74→#### Langfuse (optional)
    75→
    76→To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:
    77→
    78→```
    79→LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
    80→LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
    81→LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
    82→```
    83→
    84→When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.
    85→
    86→### Development
    87→
    88→Start both the frontend and backend:
    89→
    90→```bash
    91→make dev
    92→```
    93→
    94→Or run them separately:
    95→
    96→```bash
    97→make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
    98→make backend    # http://localhost:8000
    99→```
   100→
   101→Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.
   102→
   103→## Production Build and Deployment
   104→
   105→The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.
   106→
   107→### Build and run locally
   108→
   109→```bash
   110→docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
   111→docker run -p 10000:10000 \
   112→  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
   113→  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
   114→  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
   115→  duckdb-data-agent
   116→```
   117→
   118→Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.
   119→
   120→### Deploy to Render
   121→
   122→A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):
   123→
   124→1. Push this repo to GitHub.
   125→2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
   126→3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.
   127→
   128→Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.
   129→
   130→## Project Structure
   131→
   132→```
   133→├── frontend/               # React frontend
   134→│   ├── public/             #   Static assets (Langfuse icon)
   135→│   ├── src/
   136→│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
   137→│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling)
   138→│   │   ├── i18n/           #   Translation files (en.json, zh-TW.json)
   139→│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx #   Agent state management
   140→│   │   ├── ThemeContext.tsx #   Dark/light theme state & persistence
   141→│   │   ├── LanguageContext.tsx # i18n state, detection & translation
   142→│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
   143→│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
   144→│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
   145→│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
   146→├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
   147→│   └── app/
   148→│       ├── main.py         #   App setup & CORS
   149→│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model)
   150→│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection & query execution
   151→│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming
   152→│       ├── tracing.py      #   Langfuse client wrapper & initialization
   153→│       ├── tools.py        #   Agent SDK tool definitions (execute_sql)
   154→│       ├── data/           #   Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
   155→│       └── routes/         #   API endpoints (tables, query, chat, langfuse status)
   156→├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage production build
   157→├── render.yaml             # Render deployment config
   158→└── Makefile                # Dev commands (install, dev, clean)
   159→```
   160→
   161→## Tech Stack
   162→
   163→**Frontend**
   164→- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
   165→- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)
   166→
   167→**Backend**
   168→- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)
   169→- [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) (Python)
   170→- [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
   171→- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) (optional, for observability)
   172→
   173→## License
   174→
   175→[MIT](LICENSE.txt)
   176→

    10→def sanitize_table_name(filename: str) -> str:

    12→    sanitized = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]", "_", base.lower())

1→import duckdb
     2→import os
     3→import tempfile
     4→from typing import Any
     5→
     6→
     7→class Database:
     8→    def __init__(self):
     9→        self.conn = duckdb.connect(":memory:")
    10→
    11→    def execute_query(self, sql: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    12→        """Execute a SQL query and return results as dict with columns, rows, rowCount."""
    13→        result = self.conn.execute(sql)
    14→        if result is None:
    15→            return {"columns": [], "rows": [], "rowCount": 0}
    16→        columns = [desc[0] for desc in result.description] if result.description else []
    17→        rows = [dict(zip(columns, row)) for row in result.fetchall()] if columns else []
    18→        return {"columns": columns, "rows": rows, "rowCount": len(rows)}
    19→
    20→    def load_csv(self, file_bytes: bytes, filename: str, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    21→        """Load a CSV file into a DuckDB table. Returns table info."""
    22→        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".csv", delete=False) as tmp:
    23→            tmp.write(file_bytes)
    24→            tmp_path = tmp.name
    25→        try:
    26→            self.conn.execute(
    27→                f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(\'{tmp_path}\')'
    28→            )
    29→        finally:
    30→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    31→        return self.get_table_info(table_name)
    32→
    33→    def get_table_info(self, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    34→        """Get info about a specific table."""
    35→        cols_result = self.conn.execute(f'DESCRIBE "{table_name}"')
    36→        columns = [
    37→            {"name": row[0], "type": row[1]}
    38→            for row in cols_result.fetchall()
    39→        ]
    40→        count_result = self.conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{table_name}"')
    41→        row_count = count_result.fetchone()[0]
    42→        return {"name": table_name, "columns": columns, "rowCount": row_count}
    43→
    44→    def list_tables(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    45→        """List all tables with their schema info."""
    46→        tables_result = self.conn.execute("SHOW TABLES")
    47→        table_names = [row[0] for row in tables_result.fetchall()]
    48→        return [self.get_table_info(name) for name in table_names]
    49→
    50→    def drop_table(self, table_name: str) -> None:
    51→        """Drop a table."""
    52→        self.conn.execute(f'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "{table_name}"')
    53→
    54→    def load_sample_data(self, csv_path: str, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    55→        """Load sample CSV from a file path."""
    56→        self.conn.execute(
    57→            f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(\'{csv_path}\')'
    58→        )
    59→        return self.get_table_info(table_name)
    60→
    61→
    62→# Singleton instance
    63→db = Database()

1→import json
     2→import logging
     3→from typing import AsyncIterator
     4→
     5→from claude_agent_sdk import (
     6→    ClaudeSDKClient,
     7→    ClaudeAgentOptions,
     8→    AssistantMessage,
     9→    UserMessage,
    10→    ResultMessage,
    11→    ToolUseBlock,
    12→    ToolResultBlock,
    13→)
    14→from claude_agent_sdk.types import StreamEvent
    15→from app.tools import create_duckdb_server
    16→from app.database import db
    17→from app.config import ANTHROPIC_MODEL
    18→from app.tracing import get_langfuse_client
    19→
    20→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    21→
    22→
    23→def build_system_prompt(conversation_history: list[dict] | None = None) -> str:
    24→    tables = db.list_tables()
    25→    prompt = """You are a helpful data analyst assistant working with a DuckDB database.
    26→You can execute SQL queries using the execute_sql tool to answer questions about the user's data.
    27→
    28→Guidelines:
    29→- Write clear, efficient DuckDB SQL queries
    30→- When exploring data, start with small queries (use LIMIT)
    31→- Explain your findings in plain language after getting results
    32→- If a query fails, try to fix it and retry
    33→- Use double quotes for table and column names that might conflict with reserved words
    34→"""
    35→    if not tables:
    36→        prompt += "\nNo tables are currently loaded. Ask the user to upload a CSV file first."
    37→    else:
    38→        prompt += "\nCurrently loaded tables:\n"
    39→        for table in tables:
    40→            prompt += f'\nTable: "{table["name"]}" ({table["rowCount"]} rows)\nColumns:\n'
    41→            for col in table["columns"]:
    42→                prompt += f'  - "{col["name"]}" ({col["type"]})\n'
    43→
    44→    if conversation_history:
    45→        prompt += "\n\nPrevious conversation (for context, the user is now editing a message):\n"
    46→        for entry in conversation_history:
    47→            role = entry.get("role", "user").capitalize()
    48→            content = entry.get("content", "")
    49→            prompt += f"\n{role}: {content}\n"
    50→
    51→    return prompt
    52→
    53→
    54→def _extract_tool_result_text(content: object) -> str:
    55→    """Extract text from ToolResultBlock.content."""
    56→    if content is None:
    57→        return ""
    58→    if isinstance(content, str):
    59→        return content
    60→    if isinstance(content, list):
    61→        parts = []
    62→        for item in content:
    63→            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "text":
    64→                parts.append(item.get("text", ""))
    65→        return "\n".join(parts)
    66→    return str(content)
    67→
    68→
    69→async def stream_chat(
    70→    message: str,
    71→    session_id: str | None = None,
    72→    conversation_history: list[dict] | None = None,
    73→) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    74→    """Stream agent chat responses as SSE events."""
    75→    duckdb_server = create_duckdb_server()
    76→
    77→    logger.info("Using model: %s", ANTHROPIC_MODEL)
    78→
    79→    # Collect stderr from the CLI subprocess for debugging
    80→    stderr_lines: list[str] = []
    81→
    82→    # Use the --resume flag to continue an existing session
    83→    options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    84→        model=ANTHROPIC_MODEL,
    85→        system_prompt=build_system_prompt(conversation_history),
    86→        mcp_servers={"duckdb": duckdb_server},
    87→        allowed_tools=["mcp__duckdb__execute_sql"],
    88→        permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
    89→        max_turns=20,
    90→        include_partial_messages=True,
    91→        stderr=lambda line: stderr_lines.append(line),
    92→        **({"resume": session_id} if session_id else {}),
    93→    )
    94→
    95→    client = ClaudeSDKClient(options=options)
    96→    # Will be set from the CLI's ResultMessage; use the passed-in value until then
    97→    actual_session_id = session_id
    98→
    99→    # --- Langfuse OTel tracing setup (conditional) ---
   100→    # Deferred: session_id is set after the CLI returns it in ResultMessage
   101→    langfuse = get_langfuse_client()
   102→    observation_ctx = None
   103→    propagate_ctx = None
   104→    if langfuse:
   105→        try:
   106→            observation_ctx = langfuse.start_as_current_observation(
   107→                name="agent-chat",
   108→                input={"message": message[:500]},
   109→                metadata={"model": ANTHROPIC_MODEL},
   110→            )
   111→            observation_ctx.__enter__()
   112→
   113→            # If resuming, propagate the known session_id for child spans
   114→            if session_id:
   115→                from langfuse import propagate_attributes
   116→                propagate_ctx = propagate_attributes(session_id=session_id)
   117→                propagate_ctx.__enter__()
   118→        except Exception as e:
   119→            logger.debug("Failed to set up Langfuse tracing context: %s", e)
   120→            observation_ctx = None
   121→
   122→    try:
   123→        await client.connect()
   124→        await client.query(message, session_id=session_id or "default")
   125→
   126→        has_tool_calls = False
   127→        has_thinking = False
   128→        sql_result_ids: set[str] = set()
   129→        tool_names: dict[str, str] = {}
   130→
   131→        async for msg in client.receive_response():
   132→            if isinstance(msg, StreamEvent):
   133→                event = msg.event
   134→                event_type = event.get("type", "")
   135→
   136→                if event_type == "content_block_delta":
   137→                    delta = event.get("delta", {})
   138→                    delta_type = delta.get("type", "")
   139→                    if delta_type == "thinking_delta":
   140→                        text = delta.get("thinking", "")
   141→                        if text:
   142→                            yield f"event: thinking\ndata: {json.dumps({'text': text})}\n\n"
   143→                    elif delta_type == "text_delta":
   144→                        text = delta.get("text", "")
   145→                        event_name = "thinking" if not has_tool_calls else "answer"
   146→                        yield f"event: {event_name}\ndata: {json.dumps({'text': text})}\n\n"
   147→
   148→                elif event_type == "content_block_start":
   149→                    block = event.get("content_block", {})
   150→                    block_type = block.get("type")
   151→                    if block_type == "thinking":
   152→                        has_thinking = True
   153→                    elif block_type == "text":
   154→                        if has_thinking:
   155→                            yield f"event: thinking_done\ndata: {json.dumps({})}\n\n"
   156→                    elif block_type == "tool_use":
   157→                        has_thinking = False
   158→                        has_tool_calls = True
   159→
   160→            elif isinstance(msg, AssistantMessage):
   161→                for block in msg.content:
   162→                    if isinstance(block, ToolUseBlock):
   163→                        has_tool_calls = True
   164→                        tool_name = getattr(block, "name", "") or ""
   165→                        tool_names[block.id] = tool_name
   166→                        sql = block.input.get("sql", "")
   167→                        command = block.input.get("command", "")
   168→
   169→                        # Emit tool_call for ALL tool types
   170→                        tool_call_data: dict = {"id": block.id, "name": tool_name}
   171→                        if sql:
   172→                            tool_call_data["sql"] = sql
   173→                        if command:
   174→                            tool_call_data["command"] = command
   175→                        if not sql and not command:
   176→                            tool_call_data["input"] = block.input
   177→                        yield f"event: tool_call\ndata: {json.dumps(tool_call_data, default=str)}\n\n"
   178→
   179→                        # For SQL tools, execute query for structured results
   180→                        if sql:
   181→                            sql_result_ids.add(block.id)
   182→                            try:
   183→                                result = db.execute_query(sql)
   184→                                truncated = result["rows"][:100]
   185→                                yield f"event: tool_result\ndata: {json.dumps({'id': block.id, 'name': tool_name, 'sql': sql, 'columns': result['columns'], 'rows': truncated, 'rowCount': result['rowCount']}, default=str)}\n\n"
   186→                            except Exception as e:
   187→                                yield f"event: tool_result\ndata: {json.dumps({'id': block.id, 'name': tool_name, 'sql': sql, 'error': str(e)})}\n\n"
   188→
   189→            elif isinstance(msg, UserMessage):
   190→                # Capture tool results from the SDK for non-SQL tools
   191→                content = msg.content
   192→                if isinstance(content, list):
   193→                    for block in content:
   194→                        if isinstance(block, ToolResultBlock):
   195→                            if block.tool_use_id in sql_result_ids:
   196→                                continue
   197→                            output = _extract_tool_result_text(block.content)
   198→                            name = tool_names.get(block.tool_use_id, "")
   199→                            result_data: dict = {
   200→                                "id": block.tool_use_id,
   201→                                "name": name,
   202→                                "output": output,
   203→                            }
   204→                            if block.is_error:
   205→                                result_data["error"] = output
   206→                            yield f"event: tool_result\ndata: {json.dumps(result_data, default=str)}\n\n"
   207→
   208→            elif isinstance(msg, ResultMessage):
   209→                # Use the CLI's session_id so --resume can find it
   210→                actual_session_id = msg.session_id or actual_session_id
   211→                if msg.is_error and msg.result:
   212→                    yield f"event: error\ndata: {json.dumps({'message': msg.result})}\n\n"
   213→                yield f"event: done\ndata: {json.dumps({'session_id': actual_session_id})}\n\n"
   214→
   215→    except Exception as e:
   216→        error_msg = str(e)
   217→        if stderr_lines:
   218→            error_msg += f" | CLI stderr: {' '.join(stderr_lines[-5:])}"
   219→        logger.error("Agent error: %s", error_msg)
   220→        yield f"event: error\ndata: {json.dumps({'message': error_msg})}\n\n"
   221→    finally:
   222→        # Update trace with the CLI's session_id so Langfuse session matches
   223→        if langfuse and observation_ctx:
   224→            try:
   225→                langfuse.update_current_trace(
   226→                    session_id=actual_session_id,
   227→                    output={"session_id": actual_session_id},
   228→                )
   229→                if propagate_ctx:
   230→                    propagate_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
   231→                observation_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
   232→            except Exception as e:
   233→                logger.debug("Failed to finalize Langfuse trace: %s", e)
   234→            try:
   235→                langfuse.flush()
   236→            except Exception as e:
   237→                logger.debug("Failed to flush Langfuse: %s", e)
   238→
   239→        try:
   240→            await client.disconnect()
   241→        except Exception:
   242→            pass
   243→

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me create a detailed report of my findings. ## COMPREHENSIVE CODEBASE EXPLORATION REPORT ### 1. OVERALL PROJECT STRUCTURE This is a **SQL Playground with AI Agent** - a full-stack web application built with: **Tech Stack:** - **Frontend**: React 18 + TypeScript, Vite, CSS3 (custom properties for theming) - **Backend**: FastAPI + Uvicorn, DuckDB (in-memory SQL database), Anthropic Agent SDK - **Architecture**: React SPA with FastAPI REST API + Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming **Project Type**: Data analysis and SQL querying tool with natural language AI capabilities **Key Directories:** - `/frontend/src/` - React components and logic - `/backend/app/` - FastAPI application - `/backend/app/routes/` - API endpoint definitions - `/backend/app/data/` - Sample datasets (titanic.csv) --- ### 2. MODE SWITCHING LOGIC **Two Primary Modes:** **A. Editor Mode** (Default) - SQL query editor with manual query execution - File upload capability (CSV files, up to 500MB) - Results displayed in table or markdown format - Sample dataset loader button - Sidebar with table browser **B. Agent Mode** - Natural language chat interface - AI-powered SQL generation and execution - Session-based conversation history with edit/delete capabilities - Visible reasoning (thinking blocks, tool calls) - Real-time streaming responses via SSE **Mode Switching Implementation:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/App.tsx` (lines 146-225) ```typescript // Mode state stored in AppContent component const [agentOpen, setAgentOpen] = useState(false); // Toggle handler const handleAgentToggle = () => { setAgentOpen((prev) => !prev); }; // Conditional rendering based on agentOpen state {agentOpen ? (
{/* Agent Mode UI */}
) : (
{/* Editor Mode UI */} or
)} ``` **Button Location:** Header (top-right corner) - Shows "Agent Mode" when in editor mode (inactive button) - Shows "Editor Mode" when in agent mode (active button, `app__agent-toggle--active` class) **Recent Commits Related to Modes:** - `9d19335` (Feb 20): "feat: align editor mode layout with agent mode header and add mode label" - Added wrapper alignment and mode header labels --- ### 3. CSV UPLOAD FUNCTIONALITY **Upload UI Component:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/components/FileUpload.tsx` (lines 1-102) **Component Features:** - Drag-and-drop file upload - Click-to-select file picker - File validation (CSV only, max 500MB) - Sample dataset loader - Loading states for both upload and sample loading ```typescript // Max file size: 500MB const MAX_SIZE_BYTES = 500 * 1024 * 1024; // Validation checks if (!file.name.toLowerCase().endsWith('.csv')) { alert(t('csvOnly')); return; } if (file.size > MAX_SIZE_BYTES) { alert(t('fileTooLarge')); return; } ``` **Where Upload Component is Used:** 1. **Editor Mode** - Main content area - File: `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/App.tsx` (line 210) - Rendered inside `app__editor-wrapper` when `agentOpen === false` 2. **Props:** - `onUpload`: Callback function to handle file upload - `onLoadSample`: Callback to load Titanic dataset **Upload Data Flow:** ``` FileUpload Component ↓ handleFile() validates file ↓ onUpload callback (from App.tsx) ↓ POST /api/upload (multipart form data) ↓ Backend: tables.py upload_csv() ↓ Database: db.load_csv() ↓ Response with table metadata (name, columns, rowCount) ↓ App refreshes table list via refreshTables() ↓ Sidebar updates with new table ↓ Editor query updates to default SELECT statement ``` **Backend Upload Routes:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/backend/app/routes/tables.py` (lines 23-41) ```python @router.post("/upload") async def upload_csv(file: UploadFile = File(...)): # Validate CSV format # Sanitize filename to table name (lowercase, alphanumeric + underscore) # Call db.load_csv() with file content # Returns: {"name": table_name, "columns": [...], "rowCount": N} @router.post("/upload/sample") async def load_sample(): # Loads built-in titanic.csv from /backend/app/data/ # Same response format ``` **Table Name Sanitization:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/backend/app/routes/tables.py` (lines 10-15) ```python def sanitize_table_name(filename: str) -> str: # Remove .csv extension # Convert to lowercase, replace special chars with underscores # Ensure starts with letter or prepend "t_" # Remove consecutive underscores ``` --- ### 4. TABLE LIST FUNCTIONALITY **Table List Display - Sidebar Component:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx` (lines 1-85) **Component Features:** - Collapsible sidebar with hamburger toggle - Lists all available tables - Expandable per-table details showing: - Column names and types - Row count - Delete button for each table - Click to load table in editor **Sidebar Props:** ```typescript interface SidebarProps { tables: TableInfo[]; // Current table list onTableClick: (tableName) => void; onTableDelete: (tableName) => void; collapsed: boolean; onToggle: () => void; } ``` **State Management for Tables:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/App.tsx` (lines 230-267) ```typescript // Tables state in root App component const [tables, setTables] = useState([]); // Refresh function const refreshTables = useCallback(async () => { const response = await fetch('/api/tables'); const data = await response.json(); setTables(data); // Updates all components displaying tables }, []); // Called after: // - File upload // - Sample dataset load // - Query execution // - Table deletion ``` **Type Definitions:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/types.ts` (lines 1-10) ```typescript export interface ColumnInfo { name: string; type: string; } export interface TableInfo { name: string; columns: ColumnInfo[]; rowCount: number; } ``` **Backend Table List API:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/backend/app/routes/tables.py` (lines 18-20) ```python @router.get("/tables") async def list_tables(): return db.list_tables() # Returns list[TableInfo] ``` **Database Implementation:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/backend/app/database.py` (lines 44-48) ```python def list_tables(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: """List all tables with their schema info.""" tables_result = self.conn.execute("SHOW TABLES") table_names = [row[0] for row in tables_result.fetchall()] return [self.get_table_info(name) for name in table_names] ``` **Table Deletion:** **File:** `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/backend/app/routes/tables.py` (lines 44-47) ```python @router.delete("/tables/{table_name}") async def drop_table(table_name: str): db.drop_table(table_name) return {"ok": True} ``` **Data Flow for Table Interactions:** ``` User Clicks Table in Sidebar ↓ onTableClick(tableName) handler ↓ Sets editor query to: SELECT * FROM "tableName" LIMIT 100 ↓ Also expands table details in sidebar --- User Deletes Table ↓ onTableDelete(tableName) handler ↓ Confirmation dialog (i18n: deleteTableConfirm) ↓ DELETE /api/tables/{tableName} ↓ refreshTables() called ↓ Sidebar re-renders with updated table list ``` --- ### 5. Great, I have a clear picture. Now let me propose approaches.

## Approaches

### Approach A: Embed FileUpload directly in AgentPanel (Recommended)

- Change `agentOpen` default to `true`
- In `AgentPanel`, accept `tables`, `onUpload`, and `onLoadSample` as props
- When `tables.length === 0` and no messages exist, render `<FileUpload />` as a centered placeholder inside the message area
- When tables appear (reactive via `refreshTables`), the upload UI vanishes and normal chat empty state shows
- Reuses the exact same `FileUpload` component — no duplication

**Pros:** Minimal changes, reuses existing component, clean data flow via props from App.tsx.
**Cons:** AgentPanel gets a few more props.

### Approach B: Lift FileUpload to a shared layout layer

- Create a new wrapper component that conditionally renders FileUpload based on mode + table count
- Both editor and agent modes reference this wrapper

**Pros:** Single rendering location for FileUpload.
**Cons:** Over-engineered — adds an abstraction layer for a simple conditional. The editor mode always shows FileUpload regardless of table count, so the logic diverges anyway.

### Approach C: Use AgentContext to manage upload state

- Move upload awareness into AgentContext so the agent panel can self-manage
- AgentContext would track table state and expose upload handlers

**Pros:** Self-contained agent panel.
**Cons:** Mixes concerns — upload/table state doesn't belong in chat/agent context. More refactoring than needed.

**I recommend Approach A** — it's the simplest path with the least disruption. Does this direction sound right before I flesh out the full design?

# Agent Default Mode + CSV Upload in Agent Mode

## Summary

Make Agent Mode the default mode and allow CSV upload within Agent Mode when no tables exist.

## Changes

### 1. Default Mode: Agent Mode

In `App.tsx`, change `agentOpen` initial state from `false` to `true`:

```typescript
const [agentOpen, setAgentOpen] = useState(true);
```

### 2. FileUpload in AgentPanel

**New props on `AgentPanel`:**

```typescript
interface AgentPanelProps {
  langfuseStatus: LangfuseStatus;
  tables: TableInfo[];
  onUpload: (file: File) => Promise<void>;
  onLoadSample: () => Promise<void>;
}
```

**Conditional rendering in the message area:**

- `tables.length === 0` AND `messages.length === 0` → render `<FileUpload />`
- `tables.length > 0` AND `messages.length === 0` → render empty state text
- `messages.length > 0` → render messages (FileUpload hidden)

The FileUpload renders inside the existing `agent-panel__empty` container. Chat input remains visible at all times.

**App.tsx passes new props:**

```typescript
<AgentPanel
  langfuseStatus={langfuseStatus}
  tables={tables}
  onUpload={handleFileUpload}
  onLoadSample={handleLoadSample}
/>
```

### 3. Reactive Behavior

- Upload completes → `refreshTables()` runs → `tables` state updates → FileUpload disappears
- All tables deleted → `tables` becomes empty → FileUpload reappears (if no messages)
- No new i18n keys needed
- No backend changes needed

## Files Modified

- `frontend/src/App.tsx` — default state + prop passing
- `frontend/src/components/AgentPanel.tsx` — new props + conditional FileUpload rendering

## Verification

1. App starts in Agent Mode
2. No tables → FileUpload visible in message area
3. Upload CSV → FileUpload disappears, empty state text shows
4. Delete all tables via sidebar → FileUpload reappears
5. Chat input usable at all times
6. Editor Mode still works normally

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

**Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

**Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

**Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

**Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in plan (not "add validation")
- Exact commands with expected output
- Reference relevant skills with @ syntax
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (this session)** - I dispatch fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Parallel Session (separate)** - Open new session with executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Stay in this session
- Fresh subagent per task + code review

**If Parallel Session chosen:**
- Guide them to open new session in worktree
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** New session uses superpowers:executing-plans

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

# Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:

    **Completeness:**
    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
    - Did I miss any requirements?
    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?

    **Quality:**
    - Is this my best work?
    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
    - Is the code clean and maintainable?

    **Discipline:**
    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
    - Did I only build what was requested?
    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?

    **Testing:**
    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
    - Did I follow TDD if required?
    - Are tests comprehensive?

    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.

    ## Report Format

    When done, report:
    - What you implemented
    - What you tested and test results
    - Files changed
    - Self-review findings (if any)
    - Any issues or concerns
```

Use this template when dispatching a spec compliance reviewer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Review spec compliance for Task N"
  prompt: |
    You are reviewing whether an implementation matches its specification.

    ## What Was Requested

    [FULL TEXT of task requirements]

    ## What Implementer Claims They Built

    [From implementer's report]

    ## CRITICAL: Do Not Trust the Report

    The implementer finished suspiciously quickly. Their report may be incomplete,
    inaccurate, or optimistic. You MUST verify everything independently.

    **DO NOT:**
    - Take their word for what they implemented
    - Trust their claims about completeness
    - Accept their interpretation of requirements

    **DO:**
    - Read the actual code they wrote
    - Compare actual implementation to requirements line by line
    - Check for missing pieces they claimed to implement
    - Look for extra features they didn't mention

    ## Your Job

    Read the implementation code and verify:

    **Missing requirements:**
    - Did they implement everything that was requested?
    - Are there requirements they skipped or missed?
    - Did they claim something works but didn't actually implement it?

    **Extra/unneeded work:**
    - Did they build things that weren't requested?
    - Did they over-engineer or add unnecessary features?
    - Did they add "nice to haves" that weren't in spec?

    **Misunderstandings:**
    - Did they interpret requirements differently than intended?
    - Did they solve the wrong problem?
    - Did they implement the right feature but wrong way?

    **Verify by reading code, not by trusting report.**

    Report:
    - ✅ Spec compliant (if everything matches after code inspection)
    - ❌ Issues found: [list specifically what's missing or extra, with file:line references]
```

## Plan Alignment Analysis

### Requirement: "Show CSV upload UI in Agent Mode's empty message area when tables.length === 0"
**Status: FULLY MET**

The implementation correctly displays the FileUpload component in the empty message area with the following logic:
```tsx
{tables.length === 0 ? (
  <FileUpload onUpload={onUpload} onLoadSample={onLoadSample} />
) : (
  t('agentEmptyState')
)}
```

This condition ensures:
- FileUpload shows ONLY when no tables exist
- The original empty state message shows when tables are loaded
- Component is fully reactive - automatically updates when tables are added/removed

### Requirement: "Reuse existing FileUpload component"
**Status: FULLY MET**

- FileUpload component was properly reused from existing codebase
- No duplicate component creation
- Component already had all necessary functionality (CSV validation, drag-drop, sample loading)

### Requirement: "Reactive — disappears when tables are loaded"
**Status: FULLY MET**

- The condition `tables.length === 0` ensures the component disappears once data is loaded
- Component uses React props, automatically re-renders when tables change
- Proper reactive behavior through state management

## Code Quality Assessment

### Strengths

1. **Type Safety**: Excellent TypeScript implementation
   - Proper interface definition with all required props
   - Clear prop types: `TableInfo[]`, `(file: File) => Promise<void>`, `() => Promise<void>`
   - All type imports correctly specified

2. **Props Passing**: Clean implementation
   - App.tsx correctly passes handleFileUpload and handleLoadSample callbacks
   - Props are properly destructured in AgentPanel
   - No prop drilling issues

   - FileUpload component renders within agent-panel__empty container
   - Respects existing CSS layout structure
   - Maintains visual consistency with agent panel styling

   - File validation (CSV only)
   - File size validation (500MB limit)
   - User feedback through alerts and loading states
   - Parent component error handling through callbacks

   - All translation keys present in both en.json and zh-TW.json
   - Properly maintained: uploadDropText, uploadOr, loadSample, uploading, loading, csvOnly, fileTooLarge

   - TypeScript compilation passes without errors
   - Vite build completes successfully
   - No type errors or warnings

### Code Structure

**AgentPanel.tsx**
- 70 lines, well-organized
- Single conditional render for empty state
- Clear separation of concerns
- Proper component composition

**FileUpload.tsx**
- 102 lines, self-contained
- Proper state management for uploading/loading states
- Drag-and-drop implementation with visual feedback
- Two independent action paths: file upload and sample loading

**App.tsx**
- Correct callback implementations (lines 34-65)
- handleFileUpload includes proper error handling
- handleLoadSample includes proper error handling
- Props passed correctly to AgentPanel (lines 175-180)

## Architecture and Design Review

### Separation of Concerns
- App.tsx: Data management and API calls
- AgentPanel.tsx: Chat UI layout and message display
- FileUpload.tsx: File input UI and validation
- Clear responsibility boundaries

### Loose Coupling
- AgentPanel doesn't know implementation details of FileUpload
- FileUpload doesn't know about agent logic
- App orchestrates through callback functions
- Proper React composition pattern

### Scalability
- Easy to extend FileUpload with additional features (e.g., multiple file support)
- AgentPanel condition can be extended for other empty states
- Callback-based design allows future variations

## Documentation and Standards

### Standards Compliance
- Follows project's TypeScript conventions
- Consistent naming: camelCase for functions, PascalCase for components
- Proper import organization
- React hooks used correctly (useRef, useCallback maintained in FileUpload)

### Documentation
- Component props are clearly typed with interfaces
- No explicit JSDoc comments needed due to clear type signatures
- Code is self-documenting through clear naming and structure

## Integration Testing Considerations

The implementation should be tested for:
1. FileUpload appears when no tables exist
2. FileUpload disappears when tables are loaded
3. File upload triggers refreshTables and updates editor query
4. Sample loading works and sets editor query to titanic table
5. Drag-drop functionality works in AgentPanel context
6. Loading states display correctly
7. Error handling surfaces to user
8. i18n strings display correctly in both languages

## Issues Found

The implementation is clean, well-structured, and meets all requirements.

2. **Optional Enhancement**: Consider logging analytics when FileUpload is displayed vs when it's hidden, to track user engagement with this feature.

3. **Optional Enhancement**: Could add support for file type indicators or drag-drop hints for accessibility. Current implementation is good but could be slightly enhanced.

## Summary

**EXCELLENT IMPLEMENTATION**

The Task 2 implementation is high quality and fully meets all requirements:
- All planned functionality implemented correctly
- TypeScript types are accurate and comprehensive
- Component reuse is properly executed
- Reactive behavior works as expected
- Build succeeds without errors
- All translation keys are in place
- Error handling is robust
- Code follows project conventions

The implementation demonstrates solid understanding of React composition, proper prop management, and careful integration with existing systems. No blocking issues were found. This is production-ready code.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion → redirect → rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.
